name: Standard Scramble (Marmot Lake / O'Neil Pass approach)

waypoints.name: Duckabush Trailhead
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass required for parking; no potable water on site, nearest is Interrorem Cabin; an Olympic NP wilderness permit, reserved in advance, is needed for any overnight stay inside the park.
waypoints.directions: From Quilcene, drive south on US-101 about 15 miles to the Duckabush Recreation Area, then turn west onto Duckabush River Road/Forest Service Road 2510 and follow it about 6 miles before continuing on FS Road 2510-060 to the road-end trailhead, at about 440 feet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and there is no potable water at the trailhead (the nearest is at Interrorem Cabin); you'll also need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit, reserved in advance, if you're staying overnight inside the park. Check current Forest Service/Park Service alerts before you go, since fire-related closures and hazard-tree work in the area have affected this trail into 2026.

waypoints.name: Olympic National Park Boundary
waypoints.note: Trail #803 crosses from Olympic National Forest into Olympic National Park here, after the steep 1,000 ft climb over Big Hump; NP wilderness permit and bear-canister rules apply beyond this point.

waypoints.name: 10-Mile Camp
waypoints.note: Established riverside camp with fire rings and toilet; reliable water from the Duckabush River, but the final approach has heavy blowdown requiring scrambling around downed trees.

waypoints.name: Upper Duckabush Camp
waypoints.note: Established camp with toilet near the LaCrosse Basin trail junction; a common second-night stop before pushing on to Marmot Lake or O'Neil Pass.

waypoints.name: Marmot Lake
waypoints.note: Large subalpine lake with several established sites around the shore; the standard high camp for the summit push, about 1.3 mi and roughly 1,850 ft below Mount Duckabush's summit.

waypoints.name: O'Neil Pass (alternate high camp)
waypoints.note: Alternate high-camp/approach point 1.5 mi northeast of O'Neil Peak where the Duckabush Trail tops out; some parties stage the summit climb from here instead of Marmot Lake - not on the direct line to the summit, repositioned here as a branch off Marmot Lake rather than further along the main route.

waypoints.name: Summit ridge Class 3 steps
waypoints.note: Open talus and heather slopes above camp narrow to short, exposed Class 3 down-sloping steps just below the true summit; loose rock underfoot, use caution in wet or icy conditions.

waypoints.name: Mount Duckabush
waypoints.note: True summit (NAVD88 6,254 ft); broad views over the Duckabush and Quinault drainages and across to Mount Steel and O'Neil Peak.
